rationale: The sample is ary3 from the Shootout C++ suite, a numeric array kernel whose profile shows no debuggable source structure, meaning protection must come purely from code-level transforms; such benchmarks are dominated by a few extremely hot loops doing dense arithmetic, so the table favors cheap, semantics-preserving transforms over expensive control-flow ones. SUB and SPLIT get the strongest weights (high Security/Diversity, negligible Runtime/Size/Risk) because instruction substitution and basic-block splitting add real static-analysis friction on arithmetic-heavy code at near-zero cost; IGV is boosted to break global-value correspondence in the tight kernels with only minor cost; IBR and BCF are kept at moderate weights so they apply selectively to outer-loop or infrequently-executed blocks where their per-iteration overhead is amortized; ICALL is held back somewhat since indirect-call introduction adds dispatch overhead in hot numeric loops and carries moderate correctness risk around C++ vtable/exception edges; FLA is effectively discouraged (highest RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights, low SecurityGain) because flattening a tight array kernel would devastate the loop performance that defines this benchmark while yielding less marginal resistance than the cheaper passes already provide.
